source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Totowa campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity and 200,000 square feet of technical space, and nothing that says what density it was built for.

The operator gives no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density. Converting 6 MW at 40 kW per rack yields roughly 150 racks, and at 10 kW per rack roughly 600. The same published load supports both readings, so the spec page cannot tell a reader whether this hall is built for dense AI training or for conventional enterprise racks.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which covers controls over financial reporting. It says nothing about electrical topology, cooling method, or on-site generation, and no tenant is named. Suitability for AI compute cannot be judged from what is published here.

Within New Jersey, this campus ranks fourth by published megawatts among the five facilities in the state that publish any figure. Those five total 111.3 MW, and this campus contributes 6 MW, about five percent. The state has 48 mapped facilities, so the 111.3 MW is a floor on New Jersey's data center load, not a measure of it.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
